parsed.paper: Remarkably Early Historical Information for the Resurrection of Jesus - Gary Habermas

core_relation.sentence: The resurrection of Jesus is established as true if and only if the earliest Christian testimony (homologia, creeds, Paul's conversion, and Paul's verification with Peter and James) is both early enough and rooted in eyewitnesses, which together rule out legend or 'telephone tag'.
core_relation.quote: If Jesus was raised from the dead, Christianity is true. [S006]

product_test.quote: You get the resurrection of Jesus, as my good buddy Mike Licona says, you get the resurrection, it's game, set, and match. Christianity is true. [S011]
product_test.reason: The argument is structured so that if any one of the four early-evidence pillars (immediate preaching, early creeds, Paul's conversion, Paul's verification with eyewitnesses) is removed or shown to be late/misconstrued, the conclusion of a reliably transmitted resurrection witness collapses entirely, not merely weakens. Habermas explicitly treats the chain as a package: 'How do you know it's not phone tag? ... It rules phone tag out because he got it from the eyewitnesses.' [S412-S413]

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx: the revelatory act of God raising Jesus, which is the outside source that initiates and sustains the entire chain of testimony.
slots.quote: If Jesus was raised from the dead, Christianity is true. [S006]

slots.plays_role: Alignment: the apostolic church and Paul are aligned with the gospel kernel; the Jerusalem pillars and Paul verify they are on the same page.
slots.quote: I went to see them again, and I gave them the gospel presentation that I was preaching to see if I was running or had run in vain. [S456]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity: the transmission of the resurrection message through homologia, creeds, and Paul's testimony without distortion; 'telephone tag' is the noise the argument rules out.
slots.quote: It rules phone tag out because he got it from the eyewitnesses. [S413]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy: the tendency of oral tradition to decay into myth or misconstrued data, which the early dating and eyewitness links are meant to counteract.
slots.quote: You know how long it takes to make a myth? ... Paul was too early to be myth. Baloney. [S325-S331]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration: the compressed timeline from the cross to the creeds, Paul's conversion, and the Jerusalem meetings is the central evidence; time is the variable that makes or breaks the case.
slots.quote: How about six? ... How about six four arguments all from eyewitnesses. [S214]

slots.plays_role: Compression: the homologia and creeds are deliberately compressed, memorizable kernels that preserve the gospel for an illiterate audience.
slots.quote: Picture a sunflower seed. The kernel, the part you eat, is the homologia, but now a shell has been put around it. [S276-S277]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition: Paul's conversion on the Damascus road is a discontinuous state change from persecutor to apostle, which the argument treats as a discrete event that validates the creeds.
slots.quote: And then something happened. Boom. He meets Jesus and now magically all the creeds are true. [S296-S297]

slots.plays_role: Superposition: the open question of whether the tradition is reliable or 'telephone tag' is held unresolved until the evidence is examined; the argument aims to collapse it to one outcome.
slots.quote: How do you know we don't have homologia and creeds and Paul's testimony, but it's telephone tag? [S324]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation: the early church in Jerusalem, Paul, Peter, James, and John are correlated witnesses whose independent testimonies converge; the 'right people, right place, right time' convergence.
slots.quote: The earliest ones came out of Jerusalem, right place, within 1 to 2 years after the cross, right time, possibly or probably came from the apostles, right people, and Paul probably knew all of them. [S292]

slots.plays_role: Integration: Paul functions as the local integrator who gathers the homologia, creeds, and eyewitness testimony into a verified gospel, checking it with the pillars.
slots.quote: He goes to Jerusalem plus six, talks to James and Peter and questions them. [S441]

breaks: The paper treats the resurrection event itself (G) as a historical premise rather than a negentropy influx that must be sustained; the analogy to a continuous external source is weak.
The slot Q (superposition) is not a native category; the paper presents the evidence as already resolved, not as an open possibility awaiting actualization.
The paper adds a strong apologetic/polemical factor (defeating skeptical alternatives) that has no slot in the master equation; this is an extra dimension not captured by the product.
The emotional-doubt discussion at the end introduces a psychological factor (emotional vs. factual doubt) that is entirely outside the master-equation slots.
extra_factors: The distinction between factual and emotional doubt, and the claim that most doubts are emotional, which functions as a separate explanatory layer.
The pastoral application (be steadfast, labor not in vain) which is not part of the evidential product but is the paper's stated conclusion.
parsed.one_line: Habermas's argument is best read as a multiplicative evidential chain where early testimony, eyewitness verification, and compressed creeds must all hold together for the resurrection conclusion to stand, though several master-equation slots are only loosely mapped.
